name: __clone2
synopsis: int clone(int (*fn)(void *_Nullable), void *stack, int flags, void *_Nullable arg, ... /*pid_t *_Nullable parent_tid, void *_Nullable tls, pid_t *_Nullable child_tid */);
long syscall(SYS_clone3, struct clone_args *cl_args, size_t size);
description: Creates a new child process similar to fork(2), but with more precise control over shared execution context, such as memory, file descriptors, and signal handlers. The child process can be configured to share specific resources via flags.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: Function to be executed by the child process

parameters.name: stack
parameters.description: Pointer to the stack for the child process

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask of flags to control shared resources and behavior

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Argument passed to the function fn

parameters.name: parent_tid
parameters.description: Pointer to store the child's TID in the parent's memory (vararg)

parameters.name: tls
parameters.description: Location of the new thread-local storage (vararg)

parameters.name: child_tid
parameters.description: Pointer to store the child's TID in the child's memory (vararg)

return_value.success: Returns the thread ID of the child process
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, no child process is created, and errno is set

errors.description: CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but restrictions not met (clone3 only)
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but cgroup has a domain controller (clone3 only)
One or more PIDs in set_tid already exist (clone3 only)
Insufficient memory to create the child process
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but cgroup is invalid (clone3 only)
Insufficient permissions for namespace creation or other operations
